text:
maria: Heads-up — PR #5427 (optimize toolkit examples) is marked ready for review but there are a few blocking doc issues: the batching example is written as a big monolith, the SDK streaming snippet is missing for v2, and two external links 404. @sam can you pick up the snippet rewrite?

sam: Yep, I can take the snippets. Which streaming flavor should we show — SSE streaming via the REST SDK or the client-side WebSocket example?

maria: Let's show SSE in the main guide (most users hit it via server-side) and add an appendix with the WebSocket bit. Keep SSE minimal — show chunked responses + how to resume after an interrupt.

ben: I can do the Python SSE snippet and a cleaned batching sample. Quick question: do we want to keep the original continuous-batching config, or suggest the new "latency-preferred" preset?

jess: Recommend "latency-preferred" for the web case and show an alternate config for throughput (micro-batching) in a separate box. Also, the quant profile names changed in runtime v1.3 — docs currently reference `q4_0` and `q8_0`; the runtime team renamed them to `q4f` and `q8f` (and added `q4_1` -> `q4f_v2`) — we should add a short migration note.

maria: Good catch. Add a tiny table in the quant section: old -> new mapping + when to pick each. Keep it one paragraph.

docs-bot: link-check: /optimize/quant -> 404 (found in PR diff), /sdk/python/streaming -> 404 (referenced in examples) :warning:

sam: I'll update the links. For the SSE snippet (Python) I'd propose: 
```python
# simple SSE streaming with Redwood SDK v2
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${{REDWOOD_API_KEY}}")
with client.text.stream(model="redwood/fast-1", mode="sse") as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end="", flush=True)
```
And show how to resume using `StreamResumeToken` example line. Is that enough?

ben: That's perfect for the minimal example. For batching sample, propose splitting into two snippets: 1) production-ready `latency-preferred` with small batch size and KV-prefetch, 2) throughput `microbatch` with larger batch and prefix caching. Example config (yaml):
```yaml
# latency-preferred example
serving_config:
  batching:
    mode: latency-preferred
    max_batch_size: 8
    max_wait_ms: 15
  caching:
    kv_prefetch: true
```

```yaml
# microbatch example
serving_config:
  batching:
    mode: microbatch
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_wait_ms: 120
  caching:
    prefix_cache: true
```

jess: Also add a note about warm KV cache for short-sequence workloads — a one-liner with the sample `kv_prefetch_window` param and a link to our telemetry dashboard for hit-rate examples.

kai: I'll open a small backport PR to /v1/docs with the mapping table for quant profiles and a short note explaining that `q4f` trades a bit more quality for speed vs `q4f_v2`. I'll reference the runtime release note.

maria: Great. Action list: 
- @sam: update SSE + WebSocket appendix snippets + fix doc links (PR updates)
- @ben: split batching examples into two small snippets and add YAML configs
- @jess: add quant profile mapping paragraph + kv_prefetch note and link to telemetry
- @kai: backport mapping table to v1 docs
- @maria: final review once PRs are up; ensure CI link-check passes

sam: I'll aim to open the PR this afternoon. If anyone has a preferred wording for the resume token example, paste it here.

ben: One more micro nit — in the SDK sample we should avoid printing raw chunks in prod examples. Suggest changing `print(...)` to `emit_token(...)` in the example and include a short comment.

sam: Good call. Will update.

maria: Thanks team :tada: Let's try to land all changes within 48h so we can merge the optimize toolkit release.

docs-bot: Reminder: CI link check will re-run on push, and the docs linter enforces 80-char line wraps for code blocks.

jess: Pushed a draft for the mapping paragraph into my fork, PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5433 (will update with runtime link)

maria: ACK. Ping here when PRs are open; I'll prioritize reviews. :thumbsup:
